title: Community Garden Expands
text:
MAPLE HEIGHTS — The Maple Street Community Garden will open 24 new raised-bed plots this spring, nearly doubling its size. The expansion was made possible by a grant from the county parks department, which also paid for a new water line and a tool shed.

Plots measure 4 by 8 feet and rent for $30 per season. Residents who have never had a plot before will be given priority during the first two weeks of registration, which begins March 3. After that, any remaining plots will be offered to returning gardeners.

"We've had a waiting list for three years," said garden coordinator Ellen Ruiz. "This finally gives more neighbors a chance to grow their own food."

title: Water Shutoff Notice
text:
To: All Residents, Linden Court Apartments
From: Building Management
Subject: Water shutoff — Thursday, November 13

Dear Residents,

To replace a corroded section of the main supply pipe, water service to the entire building will be shut off on Thursday, November 13, from 9:00 AM until approximately 3:00 PM. Please store enough water in advance for drinking and cooking.

When service resumes, the water may look cloudy for a few minutes. This is harmless; simply run your cold tap until it clears. Avoid using hot water until then, as sediment can enter your water heater.

If the work is completed early, we will notify you by text.

Sincerely,
Rachel Kim, Property Manager

title: Museum Reopening
text:
Hartwell Museum Reopens After Renovation

After a two-year, $18 million renovation, the Hartwell Museum of Natural History will reopen to the public on Saturday. The project added climate-controlled galleries, which will allow the museum to display delicate items, such as pressed plants and insect specimens, that had been kept in storage for decades.

To prevent overcrowding during the first month, visitors will need timed-entry tickets, which can be reserved online up to two weeks in advance. Admission itself remains free, as it has been since the museum's founding.

Museum director Alan Pruitt said the renovation also improved accessibility. "Every gallery can now be reached by elevator," he noted, "which wasn't true before."
